summary: Haiti admits citizens of most countries visa-free for up to 90 days, collecting a USD 10 tourist fee on arrival, and CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months. Paperwork is not the obstacle here: gang violence has put most of the country, including Port-au-Prince, under do-not-travel advisories, and commercial flights are frequently suspended.

passportValidity.text: Carry a passport valid for at least six months on arrival. Given how often Haitian departures are disrupted, leaving extra validity beyond the six months is sensible.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you are arriving from, or have recently transited, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — mainly parts of tropical Africa and South America. Travelers coming directly from Europe, North America or elsewhere in the Caribbean do not need one to enter Haiti.

source.name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et des Cultes — Haiti

vaccinations.name: Hepatitis A, typhoid and routine vaccines
vaccinations.text: Not an entry condition, but hepatitis A and typhoid vaccination and up-to-date routine vaccines are strongly recommended for Haiti. Cholera has circulated since 2022 and water-borne illness is common; malaria is present year-round in much of the country.

source.name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et des Cultes — Haiti

travelInsurance.text: Not checked at the border, but comprehensive coverage including medical evacuation is essential. Read the policy wording carefully. Many insurers void coverage for countries under a government do-not-travel advisory, which now covers all of Haiti.

source.name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et des Cultes — Haiti

onwardTicket.text: Visitors are expected to hold a confirmed return or onward ticket. In practice airlines check this more consistently than immigration does.

source.name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et des Cultes — Haiti

proofOfFunds.text: No published amount. Officers may ask about your means and where you are staying, particularly if you have no local host or hotel booking.

declarations.name: Tourist fee

fee.notes: Collected on arrival. Carry it in clean US dollar notes; card payment is not reliable.

declarations.text: Visitors entering without a visa pay a USD 10 tourist fee on arrival, on top of completing the arrival card. The fee is commonly reported at USD 10 but has changed before. Carry a little extra cash in case.

source.name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et des Cultes — Haiti

declarations.name: Immigration and customs declaration card
declarations.text: A paper immigration and customs declaration is handed out on the aircraft and collected at the border. There is no official online pre-arrival form for Haiti. Treat any website charging for one as fraudulent.

source.name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et des Cultes — Haiti

currencyLimits.text: Amounts equivalent to about USD 10,000 or more in cash must be declared on arrival and departure. Given how cash-dependent Haiti is, keep receipts for any large sums you bring in.

source.name: Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et des Cultes — Haiti

notes: Firearms and ammunition are strictly prohibited. Travelers have been arrested at Port-au-Prince over a handful of forgotten rounds in a bag. Check your luggage before you fly.
Drones and satellite communication equipment can be seized without prior authorization.
Drug offenses carry heavy penalties, and Haiti is a transit route that attracts serious enforcement attention.

payments.text: Haiti runs on cash — gourdes for everyday spending, with US dollars accepted at hotels and by many traders. Cards work only at a handful of hotels and supermarkets in Port-au-Prince and Cap-Haïtien, ATMs are unreliable, and banks close for days at a time during unrest.

safety.text: Armed gangs control much of Port-au-Prince and stretches of the main roads, and kidnapping for ransom, carjacking and roadblocks are common. The US, UK and Canada all advise against all travel to Haiti. Toussaint Louverture airport has been closed to commercial traffic for extended periods since 2024. Do not travel without professional security arrangements.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Haiti Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to March is the dry, cooler season and covers Carnival in February. In practice the security situation, not the weather, decides whether travel is possible at all.

idp.text: Haiti is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Most governments advise against all travel to Haiti. Gangs control roads around Port-au-Prince — including the route to the airport — and foreigners have been kidnapped for ransom. Anyone traveling for work should have professional security and evacuation arrangements in place before arrival.

Commercial flights to Port-au-Prince have been repeatedly suspended since 2024, with US carriers barred from the airport for long stretches after aircraft were hit by gunfire. Cap-Haïtien is sometimes the only usable air link — reconfirm your route in the days before departure, not weeks ahead.
Visa-free visitors pay a USD 10 tourist fee at the airport on arrival. Bring it in clean, undamaged US dollar notes — card terminals are unreliable and there is no way around the fee.
Prices are often quoted in "Haitian dollars", an informal unit worth five gourdes and not a real currency. Always confirm whether a price is in gourdes, Haitian dollars or US dollars before paying.
Register with your embassy before arrival, keep a charged phone with roaming or satellite capability, and do not rely on local mobile networks or mains power being available.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Haiti?
faq.answer: Usually not. Haiti admits citizens of most countries — including the EU, UK, US, Canada and the Commonwealth — visa-free for up to 90 days, with a USD 10 tourist fee paid on arrival. CARICOM nationals get six months. A short list of nationalities, among them mainland Chinese, Colombian, Cuban and Dominican passport holders, must obtain a visa from a Haitian mission first; confirm with the embassy before booking, as Haiti's list is not widely published.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel to Haiti in 2026?
faq.answer: No, and that is the central fact about visiting Haiti right now. The US, UK and Canada all advise against all travel because of gang control of Port-au-Prince and much of the country, widespread kidnapping and armed roadblocks. Visa rules are the easy part; getting in, moving around and getting out safely is not.

faq.question: How much is Haiti's tourist fee?
faq.answer: USD 10 per visitor, collected in cash on arrival from travelers entering without a visa. It is separate from any airline taxes and from the departure fee usually built into your ticket. Carry it in US dollar notes.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Haiti without a visa?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days for most nationalities, with the officer writing the actual period on your stamp. Extensions are handled by the Direction de l'Immigration et de l'Émigration in Port-au-Prince, which is not always functioning normally — do not plan a stay that depends on getting one.

faq.question: Are flights to Haiti operating?
faq.answer: Intermittently. Port-au-Prince has been closed to commercial flights for long stretches since 2024, and services from the US have been suspended and resumed several times. Cap-Haïtien in the north is sometimes the only viable airport. Check your airline's status days before departure, and expect cancellations.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Haiti?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from or transit a yellow fever risk country in tropical Africa or South America. More relevant for most travelers are hepatitis A and typhoid vaccination, malaria prophylaxis and strict care with water — cholera has circulated in Haiti since 2022.
